block_node.block_desc:
Read and output recorded IO data from hardware.
The block outputs a message containing IO device data. To access the data, connect the data output to a device driver block like UDP Read, TCP Read, Stream Read or Register Read and place the block in your application algorithm.
Set the Input parameter to 'From File' to play back data from a recorded file. Set the Input parameter to 'From dialog' and set the Value parameter to specify the input data. Set the Input to 'From input port' to receive data and signals from the input ports. Set the Input to 'From timeseries object' to input data and time values using timeseries object created in MATLAB. Set the Device type parameter to 'Stream' and set the Number of buffers parameter to specify the queue length.

Capture IO data from hardware.
The block accepts data from a device driver block like UDP Write, TCP Write, or Register Write. The block outputs, records or terminates the received data.
Set the Output parameter to 'To file' to save the data to a file. Set the Dataset name parameter to the desired filename.

Output event.
The block outputs a message indicating an event. The event can be used to trigger a Task Manager event-driven task.
Set the Input parameter to 'From dialog' and set the Sample time parameter to generate events periodically. Set the Input to 'From input port' to receive event trigger from the input port. Set the Input to 'From timeseries object' to generate events using timeseries object created in MATLAB.

Represents the effects of a task that is not part of your application. This block can be used to model the impact of a task that will compete for the processor time with your application.
The block should be matched to a task in the Task Manager. The code is not generated for the testbench task.
